name: stall_class_mapping
kind: calibration of configs/stall/class_mapping.json (engine stall-ledger reason -> ncu warp-stall class). No new probe: the single-mechanism probe kernels that already exist as replay rows are run once more under ncu warp-stall sampling and replayed by the engine with --stall-ledger. No timing leaf and no engine timing rule comes out of this protocol.
question: For each engine stall reason: which ncu sample class does hardware report for the wait at the place where the engine charges that reason? A rule of the mapping becomes `calibrated` only from these probe kernels, never from a suite case.
motivation: dev/design/stall-attribution.md section 4. The first full-GPU comparison (H100, 495 cases, engine ledger of the first wave) has a mean attribution error of 0.71 of the hardware residency under the all-hypothesis mapping against 0.079 mean cycle error; the two largest (region, class) gaps are loop/gmma (+14.5 % of residency, engine only) and loop/barrier (-13.0 %, hardware only), i.e. a mapping question before it is a mechanism question.
data_seen_before_freezing: H100 suite-level reason/class co-occurrence from the first-wave ledgers (~/tmp/acc-look/ledger1b/hp/reason_classes.tsv, 495 full-GPU cases): arch:warpgroup_wait overlaps barrier 0.63, cta_barrier barrier 0.70, cluster_barrier barrier 0.995, semantic:mbarrier_wait long_scoreboard 0.76, reg:LDG:* long_scoreboard 0.68-0.76, reg:ULDC:miss imc_miss 0.59, suspended:sleep sleeping 0.66, exit_drain drain 0.63, control_floor split (wait 0.26, barrier 0.22, long_scoreboard 0.19).

Per-pc listing of cublas_bf16_bigK_00 (H100): hardware reports `barrier` at WARPGROUP.DEPBAR and at the instruction after a CTA barrier, `mio_throttle` at HGMMA, `long_scoreboard` at the NANOSLEEP / BRA after a failed SYNCS try-wait; the engine charges the try-wait at the SYNCS instruction itself.
Counters against samples on 75 dense-sampled cases of another line ($A/stall-compare/hw-dense): the counter class `gmma` is never present in the samples.

Second-wave ledgers (H100 499 cases, B300 266): the per-pc issue counts of the two sides differ only in spin-wait loops (BLF-BF16-C13: one try-wait loop runs 62731 iterations under ncu sampling and 2083 in the traced run); hence the same_launch control leaves spin-wait runs out. Hardware parks a waiting warp at the barrier / nanosleep instruction itself while the engine ledger of that wave keyed the wait at the following instruction; the ledger is changed to key post-issue blocks at the blocking instruction before the probe rows are run.

These observations are suite data. They are recorded here because they were seen; they do not decide any rule. The predictions below are the hypothesis mapping as committed (configs/stall/class_mapping.json at ba0286ee) plus one explicit doubt.
probe: H100: every row of suites/hopper/microbench/cases.tsv (replay rows of overlap_v4 [wgmma], fp_stream_mix, alu_forms, store_flood, tma_oob, gather_hit, math_occupancy, load_after_copies, arrive_status; binaries already built under $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT as the rows name them). Per row: (1) tracer capture of the row's launch (`cyclescope capture --suite hopper/microbench --mode trace`); (2) hardware: scripts/pipeline/stall_reference_batch.sh on the same suite, sampling interval 0, launch pinned to the traced launch; (3) engine: convert -> build -> simulate with --stall-ledger (convert_capture_batch.sh STALL_LEDGER=1, h100 tree of the branch); (4) `cyclescope stall compare` + `cyclescope stall summarize`. B300 has no microbench suite rows yet: version 1 calibrates H100 only and the B300 rules stay `hypothesis`.

controls.same_launch: a row is usable only when the per-pc issue counts agree (execution_count_error <= 0.05, counted over the pcs outside spin-wait runs: straight-line runs holding a SYNCS try-wait or a NANOSLEEP), the listing agrees (mnemonic_mismatches == 0) and warps_ratio is within 2 % of 1.
controls.reference: reference_consistency <= 0.10 and at least 2000 samples; rows below are reported as `thin` and not used.
controls.timing: cycle_ratio within 0.85-1.15. A probe whose time is wrong is a mechanism finding (own protocol), not a mapping row; it is reported and not used.
controls.repeat: the hardware pass is run twice for every row; class shares of the two runs within 3 points, else the row is `unstable` and not used.

derivation: Per usable row the co-occurrence of cyclescope.stall.compare (per straight-line run of pcs, the overlapping wait cycles min(hardware, engine) spread over (reason, class) by both sides' shares; `issued` / `selected` excluded). Pooled over usable rows with every row weighted by its own hardware residency. For a reason r: share(r, c) = pooled overlap of (r, c) / pooled overlap of r. Reasons are pooled by rule of the mapping (all reasons one rule matches form one line) and also listed singly.

predictions_before_data.hypothesis_mapping: every rule's class in configs/stall/class_mapping.json at ba0286ee is the prediction for the reasons it matches.
predictions_before_data.doubt: arch:* -> gmma is expected to fail: ncu's samples have no gmma class, so the samples must put a warpgroup wait somewhere else (barrier, long_scoreboard or wait).
predictions_before_data.no_prediction: control_floor, fetch, operand_collector, unit:* (which of not_selected / dispatch_stall / math_pipe_throttle / mio_throttle hardware reports for an execution-unit wait).

outcomes_before_data.per_rule: For every mapping rule whose reasons reach a pooled overlap of at least 1 % of the pooled hardware residency in at least two usable rows: (A) top class share >= 0.70 -> the rule maps to that class and becomes `calibrated` with source `stall_class_mapping.h100.v1`; when the class differs from the hypothesis the rule changes; (B) top share < 0.70 -> the rule keeps its class and stays `hypothesis`; the shares are reported as a split. A split is not resolved by adding suite-specific rules; it may be resolved by a more specific reason from the engine (a later protocol version). (C) not reached -> stays `hypothesis`, listed as not exercised.
outcomes_before_data.unusable_rows: rows failing a control are listed with the failed control; rows with cycle_ratio outside the band are handed over as mechanism findings.

not_allowed: No engine timing change, no leaf, no mapping change justified by a suite case, no change of the 0.70 / 1 % / two-row thresholds after the data is seen (an addendum may add probes, not move thresholds).

addenda.when: before any probe row was replayed by the engine
addenda.text: The ledger keying named in data_seen_before_freezing (post-issue blocks at the blocking instruction) was revised from hardware-only evidence over the full-GPU reference: ncu barrier samples sit on the instruction after BAR and on UCGABAR_WAIT itself, sleeping samples on the instruction after NANOSLEEP. The ledger keys cta_barrier and suspended:sleep at the next instruction to issue, cluster_barrier and the other suspensions at the suspending instruction. The derivation pools per straight-line run, so thresholds and outcomes are unchanged.

addenda.when: h100 run of version 1 (engine build b3fb43de, ledger keying of 8d315859)
addenda.text: 77 rows captured, measured twice and replayed ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/calibration/h100: compare-a, compare-b, table/calibration.json). Row status: 13 usable, 49 thin (fewer than 2000 samples or reference_consistency above 0.10; the probe kernels are short), 6 same_launch (4 tma_oob rows with warps_ratio 1.10-1.16 and reference_consistency 0.21-0.35; 2 wgmma solo rows), 6 timing (cycle_ratio 1.22 on the three grp2r d600 rows, 0.51-0.82 on three store_flood rows: handed over as mechanism findings), 3 unstable. Three usable rows (mb-rowg-single-l1 / l8 / l32) were captured with a launch-table override because the mangled kernel name in suites/hopper/microbench/launches.tsv does not match the deployed binary; the decisions below hold without them. Decisions: (A) reg:LDG:* -> long_scoreboard (11 rows, share 0.90) and scoreboard_slot -> long_scoreboard (5 rows, share 0.85) become calibrated; the two mapping rules were split so that only the reasons the usable rows exercised carry the evidence (async_group_wait and the other long-latency producers of the same rules stay hypothesis). (B) split, class kept, hypothesis: issue_slot (math_pipe_throttle 0.38 / wait 0.29 / not_selected 0.28), unit:* (math_pipe_throttle 0.44 / wait 0.25 / not_selected 0.24, almost all unit:fmaheavy_smsp), control_floor (long_scoreboard 0.40 / wait 0.39 / short_scoreboard 0.13), reg:<other> (wait 0.58 / short_scoreboard 0.22). (C) not reached: every other rule, among them arch:*, cta_barrier / cluster_barrier, the mbarrier waits, sleep, fetch, exit_drain and the store rules: their probe rows are thin, same_launch or timing. Observation only, not a decision: on the thin wgmma rows the overlap of arch:warpgroup_wait is mostly with `barrier` (the doubt written before the data), cta_barrier with `barrier`, store_buffer / store_issue_interval with lg_throttle, unit:xu_smsp with mio_throttle. A later version needs probe rows long enough for 2000 samples (more repetitions per launch) before these rules can be decided.

addenda.when: before any data of the longer rows (version 2 rows)
addenda.text: Version 1 could not decide most rules because the probe kernels are too short for 2000 samples (one sample per about 35 kernel cycles on one SM). Added rows, thresholds and derivation unchanged: for every version-1 row with fewer than 2000 samples whose command line has an in-kernel repetition count (`--reps`; `--iters` for gather) a row `<id>-long` (set `stallmap`) with the same command line and repetitions = min(256, ceil(old x 8000 / version-1 samples)). A repetition argument that adds launches instead of lengthening the profiled launch does not qualify (row not added, recorded). Rows without such an argument and rows that failed version 1 for another reason with 2000 samples or more are not re-run. The version-2 table pools the version-1 usable rows with the usable `-long` rows; a `-long` row replaces nothing.

addenda.when: h100 run of the version 2 rows (engine build b3fb43de)
addenda.text: 42 `-long` rows added (the version-1 rows under 2000 samples that have an in-kernel repetition count), captured, measured twice and replayed ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/calibration/h100-long; pooled table h100-v2/table). Of the 42: 32 usable (4000-10000 samples, cycle_ratio 0.85-1.15), 6 timing (gather w1 x2 0.81 / 0.85, grp2r d150 x3 1.19-1.21, seq3 0.73: mechanism findings), 3 unstable, 1 thin (reference_consistency 0.29). Pooled with version 1: 119 rows, 45 usable. Decisions: (A) cta_barrier -> barrier (35 rows, share 0.81): calibrated; cluster_barrier was not exercised and stays hypothesis (rule split). (A, class changes) arch:warpgroup_wait -> barrier (17 rows, share 0.76; wait 0.13, mio_throttle 0.06): the hypothesis gmma is replaced for this reason, as the doubt written before the data expected; the other arch:* reasons had no overlap to speak of (arch:wgmma_rendezvous 0.07 against 8.3 cycles-per-residency units) and stay hypothesis. (A) reg:LDL:* -> long_scoreboard (6 rows, share 0.94): calibrated (rule split from the long-latency producers). reg:LDG:* unchanged (11 rows, 0.90). scoreboard_slot keeps its version-1 decision: its shares are unchanged (0.85 long_scoreboard, the same 5 rows) but its overlap is now 0.7 % of the larger pooled residency, under the 1 % line; adding unrelated rows cannot un-decide a rule, and no rule is decided on less than the line by this reading. (B) split, hypothesis kept: issue_slot (not_selected 0.28 / math_pipe_throttle 0.26 / wait 0.17), unit:* (mio_throttle 0.25 / wait 0.25 / not_selected 0.17 / math_pipe_throttle 0.13; unit:xu_smsp overlaps mio_throttle, the ALU / FMA units math_pipe_throttle and not_selected), operand_collector (not_selected 0.30 / dispatch_stall 0.22), control_floor (wait 0.32 / barrier 0.29 / long_scoreboard 0.14), the short-latency producers reg:LDC / ULDC / MUFU (wait 0.30 / barrier 0.29 / short_scoreboard 0.12). (C) under the line: the store rules (0.4 %), the remaining reg:*. Not exercised by any usable row: the mbarrier waits, sleep, fetch, exit_drain, async_group_wait, cluster_barrier, memory_queue, gsync. B300 has no probe rows; its rules are the H100 ones with the same evidence labels, which for B300 are hypotheses.
